diagnosis: The FIFO incorrectly publishes frames after reset because the read-side state (rd_ptr_reg, mem_read_data_valid_reg) is not initialized, causing garbage data to appear valid immediately. Simultaneously, the write-side pointer (wr_ptr_cur_reg) is not reset, so the FRAME_FIFO logic misinterprets the frame boundary and asserts m_axis_tvalid for three cycles with stale data.

proposal.diagnosis: The FIFO incorrectly publishes frames after reset because the read-side state (rd_ptr_reg, mem_read_data_valid_reg) is not initialized, causing garbage data to appear valid immediately. Simultaneously, the write-side pointer (wr_ptr_cur_reg) is not reset, so the FRAME_FIFO logic misinterprets the frame boundary and asserts m_axis_tvalid for three cycles with stale data.

ranking.mechanism: Resets rd_ptr_reg and mem_read_data_valid_reg in the read-side always_ff block, eliminating stale read pointers and invalid data valid flags that cause m_axis_tvalid to assert prematurely.
Resets rd_addr_reg in the same block, ensuring the memory read address starts from a known state and does not fetch garbage on the first read after reset.
Resets wr_addr_reg in the write-side always_ff block, guaranteeing the first accepted frame is written to address 0 and aligns with the cleared read pointer.
Resets m_axis_reg so the output register does not drive stale frame payload onto m_axis_tdata/m_axis_tlast while m_axis_tvalid is incorrectly high.
Qualifies s_axis_tready with !rst, preventing the write logic from accepting input during the reset cycle and avoiding pointer updates that would corrupt frame tracking.
